newsitem.title: USA: Forest Oil adds to U.S. Gulf portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Forest Oil adds to U.S. Gulf portfolio.

text.p: Forest Oil Corp on Thursday said it was the high bidder on eight of 12 bids it submitted in Wednesday's record-setting auction of rights to drill in federal waters off the coast of Louisiana.

The Denver-based company submitted high bids totalling $6.2 million on Gulf of Mexico tracts, including a $3.9 million bid for Eugene Island Block 43 located near a Forest-operated production platform.

Four of its winning bids were on tracts in water depths between 600 feet (183 metres) and 1,000 feet (305 metres), part of a strategy of building a portfolio of prospects in the deeper water slope area to complement a traditional position on the shelf, the company said.
Bids in the lease round are subject to final approval of the U.S. Minerals Management Service, a Department of the Interior agency which regulates drilling in federal waters of the Gulf of Mexico.
A record 1,790 bids were submitted as producers anted up a total $1.24 billion in the auction, making the sale the most active lease round in terms of dollars bid since 1985.
